title: Forklift truck operations, traveling and loading practice questions
description: Practice questions on OSHA forklift truck operations, traveling and loading: unattended trucks, docks, grades, elevators, tilting loads (29 CFR 1910.178).

questions.question: An employee is standing in front of a workbench. What does 1910.178(m)(1) say about driving a truck toward that employee?

options.A: The truck may approach if the horn is sounded first
options.B: Trucks shall not be driven up to anyone standing in front of a bench or other fixed object
options.C: The truck may approach at walking speed
options.D: The truck may approach if the forks are fully lowered

questions.explanation: Paragraph (m)(1) states: "Trucks shall not be driven up to anyone standing in front of a bench or other fixed object."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Trucks shall not be driven up to anyone standing in front of a bench or other fixed object.

questions.question: A truck's forks are raised but carry no load. What does 1910.178(m)(2) say about a worker walking under the elevated forks?

options.A: It is allowed because the truck is empty
options.B: It is allowed if the worker passes without stopping
options.C: It is allowed once the operator has neutralized the controls
options.D: No person shall be allowed to pass under the elevated portion of the truck, whether loaded or empty

questions.explanation: "No person shall be allowed to stand or pass under the elevated portion of any truck, whether loaded or empty." The rule covers both standing and passing, and an empty truck is included.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: No person shall be allowed to stand or pass under the elevated portion of any truck, whether loaded or empty.

questions.question: When a load is picked up, how far does 1910.178(o)(5) say the load engaging means shall be placed under the load?

options.A: As far as possible
options.B: Halfway under the load
options.C: Only far enough to lift the load clear of the floor
options.D: Exactly to the load's center

questions.explanation: "A load engaging means shall be placed under the load as far as possible; the mast shall be carefully tilted backward to stabilize the load."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A load engaging means shall be placed under the load as far as possible; the mast shall be carefully tilted backward to stabilize the load.

questions.question: Under 1910.178(m)(4), where shall the employer prohibit arms or legs from being placed?

options.A: Over the load backrest extension
options.B: Above the overhead guard
options.C: Between the uprights of the mast or outside the running lines of the truck
options.D: Against the steering wheel while traveling

questions.explanation: "The employer shall prohibit arms or legs from being placed between the uprights of the mast or outside the running lines of the truck." The duty falls on the employer.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The employer shall prohibit arms or legs from being placed between the uprights of the mast or outside the running lines of the truck.

questions.question: An operator gets off the truck and walks behind a rack, so the truck is no longer in his view, though it is only about 10 ft. away. How does 1910.178(m)(5)(ii) classify the truck?

options.A: As unattended, because the operator left the vehicle and it is not in his view
options.B: As attended, because the operator is less than 25 ft. away
options.C: As attended until the operator is 25 ft. or more away
options.D: As unattended only if the engine is still running

questions.explanation: A truck is unattended "when the operator is 25 ft. or more away from the vehicle which remains in his view, or whenever the operator leaves the vehicle and it is not in his view." Once it is out of view, distance does not matter.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A powered industrial truck is unattended when the operator is 25 ft. or more away from the vehicle which remains in his view, or whenever the operator leaves the vehicle and it is not in his view.

questions.question: A truck will be left unattended on an incline. Besides fully lowering the load engaging means, neutralizing the controls, shutting off power and setting the brakes, what does 1910.178(m)(5)(i) require?

options.A: Turning the steering wheel fully to one side
options.B: Blocking the wheels
options.C: Raising the load engaging means slightly off the floor
options.D: Leaving the warning lights on

questions.explanation: After the steps for any unattended truck, the rule adds: "Wheels shall be blocked if the truck is parked on an incline."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Wheels shall be blocked if the truck is parked on an incline.

questions.question: Besides keeping a safe distance from the edge of ramps or platforms, what does 1910.178(m)(6) say trucks shall not be used for?

options.A: Driving onto a semitrailer
options.B: Moving loads into freight cars
options.C: Crossing railroad tracks
options.D: Opening or closing freight doors

questions.explanation: Paragraph (m)(6) states: "Trucks shall not be used for opening or closing freight doors."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Trucks shall not be used for opening or closing freight doors.

questions.question: When does 1910.178(m)(7) say fixed jacks may be necessary to support a semitrailer during loading or unloading?

options.A: When the trailer is coupled to a tractor
options.B: Whenever the trailer flooring has been checked
options.C: When the trailer is not coupled to a tractor
options.D: Only when the trailer is parked on a grade

questions.explanation: "Fixed jacks may be necessary to support a semitrailer during loading or unloading when the trailer is not coupled to a tractor." The rule says "may be necessary", not "shall".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Fixed jacks may be necessary to support a semitrailer during loading or unloading when the trailer is not coupled to a tractor.

questions.question: According to 1910.178(m)(9), what is an overhead guard not intended to withstand?

options.A: The impact of small packages
options.B: The impact of boxes
options.C: The impact of bagged material
options.D: The impact of a falling capacity load

questions.explanation: An overhead guard "is intended to offer protection from the impact of small packages, boxes, bagged material, etc., representative of the job application, but not to withstand the impact of a falling capacity load."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: an overhead guard is intended to offer protection from the impact of small packages, boxes, bagged material, etc., representative of the job application, but not to withstand the impact of a falling capacity load.

questions.question: Under 1910.178(m)(10), a load backrest extension shall be used whenever necessary to minimize the possibility of what?

options.A: The load or part of it falling rearward
options.B: The truck tipping sideways in a turn
options.C: Objects from above striking the operator
options.D: The truck rolling while parked

questions.explanation: "A load backrest extension shall be used whenever necessary to minimize the possibility of the load or part of it from falling rearward."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A load backrest extension shall be used whenever necessary to minimize the possibility of the load or part of it from falling rearward.

questions.question: What following distance from the truck ahead does 1910.178(n)(1) set?

options.A: Approximately one truck length
options.B: Approximately two truck lengths
options.C: Approximately three truck lengths
options.D: Approximately six truck lengths

questions.explanation: "A safe distance shall be maintained approximately three truck lengths from the truck ahead, and the truck shall be kept under control at all times."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A safe distance shall be maintained approximately three truck lengths from the truck ahead

questions.question: A truck operator meets an ambulance responding to an emergency in the plant. What does 1910.178(n)(2) require?

options.A: Continuing at the authorized plant speed limit
options.B: Yielding the right of way to the ambulance
options.C: Sounding the horn and passing the ambulance
options.D: Following the ambulance at three truck lengths

questions.explanation: "The right of way shall be yielded to ambulances, fire trucks, or other vehicles in emergency situations."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The right of way shall be yielded to ambulances, fire trucks, or other vehicles in emergency situations.

questions.question: Another truck ahead is traveling in the same direction through a blind spot. What does 1910.178(n)(3) say about passing it?

options.A: It shall not be passed
options.B: It may be passed if the horn is sounded
options.C: It may be passed at a reduced speed
options.D: It may be passed if the other driver waves the truck by

questions.explanation: "Other trucks traveling in the same direction at intersections, blind spots, or other dangerous locations shall not be passed."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Other trucks traveling in the same direction at intersections, blind spots, or other dangerous locations shall not be passed.

questions.question: 1910.178(n)(5) prohibits parking a truck closer than 8 feet from what?

options.A: The nearest rail
options.B: The edge of the railroad crossing
options.C: The nearest railroad car
options.D: The center of railroad tracks

questions.explanation: "Parking closer than 8 feet from the center of railroad tracks is prohibited."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Parking closer than 8 feet from the center of railroad tracks is prohibited.

questions.question: A loaded truck has to go down a grade in excess of 10 percent. Under 1910.178(n)(7)(i), how shall it be driven?

options.A: With the load downgrade
options.B: With the load upgrade
options.C: With the load raised high enough to see under it
options.D: Diagonally across the grade

questions.explanation: "When ascending or descending grades in excess of 10 percent, loaded trucks shall be driven with the load upgrade." This applies to loaded trucks going either up or down such grades.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: When ascending or descending grades in excess of 10 percent, loaded trucks shall be driven with the load upgrade.

questions.question: Before a truck is driven over a dockboard or bridgeplate, what does 1910.178(n)(11) require?

options.A: That the truck be unloaded
options.B: That the operator sound the horn twice
options.C: That the dockboard or bridgeplate be properly secured
options.D: That the truck travel with the load trailing

questions.explanation: "Dockboard or bridgeplates, shall be properly secured before they are driven over." They are then driven over "carefully and slowly and their rated capacity never exceeded."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Dockboard or bridgeplates, shall be properly secured before they are driven over.

questions.question: A truck has just entered an elevator. What does 1910.178(n)(12) require once it is on the elevator?

options.A: The load raised to clear the elevator door
options.B: The truck turned to face the door
options.C: The controls neutralized, power shut off, and the brakes set
options.D: The operator dismounted and off the elevator

questions.explanation: "Once on the elevator, the controls shall be neutralized, power shut off, and the brakes set."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Once on the elevator, the controls shall be neutralized, power shut off, and the brakes set.

questions.question: 1910.178(n)(15) says the hand steering wheel shall be turned at a moderate, even rate, except in what case?

options.A: When maneuvering at a very low speed
options.B: When the truck is not carrying a load
options.C: When traveling with the load trailing
options.D: When the turn is at a cross aisle

questions.explanation: "Except when maneuvering at a very low speed, the hand steering wheel shall be turned at a moderate, even rate."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Except when maneuvering at a very low speed, the hand steering wheel shall be turned at a moderate, even rate.

questions.question: A load is off-center and cannot be centered. What does 1910.178(o)(1) say about handling it?

options.A: It shall not be handled
options.B: It may be handled only with a vertical load backrest extension
options.C: It may be handled only on level floors
options.D: Caution shall be exercised when handling it

questions.explanation: "Only stable or safely arranged loads shall be handled. Caution shall be exercised when handling off-center loads which cannot be centered."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Caution shall be exercised when handling off-center loads which cannot be centered.

questions.question: An operator is holding an elevated load. Under 1910.178(o)(6), when may that load be tilted forward?

options.A: Whenever the mast was first tilted fully back
options.B: When the load is in a deposit position over a rack or stack
options.C: When the truck is traveling down a grade
options.D: Whenever a load backrest extension is in place

questions.explanation: "An elevated load shall not be tilted forward except when the load is in a deposit position over a rack or stack."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.178, Powered industrial trucks (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: An elevated load shall not be tilted forward except when the load is in a deposit position over a rack or stack.
